matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After proposing a transformed equation, compute the integer values of both sides using standard Roman numerals to ensure the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you have a candidate transformed equation, before finalizing, verify the arithmetic correctness.
matchstick.example: Skipping the arithmetic check and accepting a transformed equation that does not actually balance (e.g., believing XIII - XI = II is correct without confirming 13‑11=2).

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you may only place it where the same orientation is appropriate for the target character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick, ensure the destination character can accept a stick of that orientation without becoming an invalid shape.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick onto a vertical I, creating an invalid character that mixes orientations.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect at most the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick); no other characters may change.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any transformation, track that only two characters are altered.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from ‘=’ and adding it to ‘+’, but also inadvertently changing a numeral elsewhere, violating the one‑stick rule.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: Use known one‑stick transformations (e.g., I↔II, V↔X) that keep both source and destination characters valid Roman numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a numeral needs to change and a stick can be moved from another character without breaking either shape.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I to a V but leaving the source I empty, resulting in an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final output must be a single line that starts with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the transformed equation, with uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After finding a valid transformation, format the answer exactly as required before returning it.
matchstick.example: Returning the equation without the required prefix or with extra spaces, causing the verifier to reject the answer.

matchstick.title: Accurate parsing of the original equation
matchstick.principle: Read the given equation carefully and record each numeral and operator exactly as they appear before attempting any modifications.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, before planning any stick moves.
matchstick.example: Misreading ‘XI - II = IX’ as ‘XI = II - IX’, leading to an incorrect transformation plan.

matchstick.title: Within‑character diagonal repositioning
matchstick.principle: You may relocate a diagonal stick within the same numeral, effectively turning X into V (or V into X) without moving sticks between characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a numeral contains diagonal sticks that can be rearranged to form another valid numeral.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn X into V by removing a diagonal stick entirely, leaving an invalid single‑diagonal character.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a ‘‑’ creates a ‘+’, and removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ yields a ‘‑’, changing the operator while preserving orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a plus or minus sign and a vertical stick is available to transfer.
matchstick.example: Removing a vertical stick from ‘+’ but forgetting to change the ‘+’ to ‘‑’, leaving an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer from '+' to numeral (adds I)
matchstick.principle: When moving a vertical stick from a ‘+’ operator, the ‘+’ becomes ‘‑’, and the removed stick can be added to a numeral, effectively inserting an I.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation has a ‘+’ and a numeral that can accept an extra vertical stick to become a valid larger numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from ‘+’ to a V but forgetting to change the ‘+’ to ‘‑’, resulting in an unchanged plus sign.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via horizontal stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Moving a horizontal stick between operators can swap an ‘=’ and a ‘‑’: removing one of the two horizontal sticks from ‘=’ turns it into ‘‑’, and adding that stick to a ‘‑’ turns it into ‘=’.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation contains both an equals sign and a minus sign, consider moving a horizontal stick from one to the other to adjust the operators.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from ‘=’ to ‘‑’ but leaving the original ‘=’ with a single horizontal line (invalid) or the ‘‑’ with two lines (invalid).

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes the transformed equation is correct without checking the numeric values of both sides.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the integer values of the left‑ and right‑hand sides after any transformation and confirm they are equal.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving a stick, the source or destination character may lose or gain a stick in a way that no longer matches any Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that both the character losing a stick and the character gaining a stick still correspond to a valid Roman numeral or operator.

matchstick.why_it_happens: A stick move may change an operator into a shape that is not a recognized operator (e.g., a ‘=’ with one line, or a ‘‑’ with two lines).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that after moving sticks, any modified operator matches one of the allowed symbols (+, -, =).

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character but does not place it onto another character, violating the rule that a stick must be relocated.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Track the stick’s movement and verify that it is added to a valid destination character.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The final line does not follow the exact required prefix or whitespace rules, causing the verifier to miss the answer.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Produce a single line that begins with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the equation, with uppercase letters and no extra spaces.
